thread.title: Apple to Take 25% Stake in…Itself?

author: Jack Hough
title: Apple to Take 25% Stake in…Itself?
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) could buy back 25% of its stock over the next three years as it brings home foreign cash, according to a new analysis from UBS analyst Steven Milunovich . That buying is likely to provide support for shares as iPhone unit growth slows , and services and other businesses play a more important role.
Illustration: Justin Sullivan/Getty Images A U.S. corporate tax overhaul allows--forces, really--companies to repatriate foreign cash at a tax rate much lower than the one they would have paid under the old system. That’s highly relevant to Apple, which ended last year with $252 billion in overseas cash and investments .
Of course, it won’t spend all of that on stock and dividends. For one thing, Apple holds $97 billion in long-term debt issued at favorable interest rates. Milunovich reckons it likes to keep $90 billion in net cash and investments on hand. But by his math, Apple has been managing its cash with the assumption that it would pay a 25% tax to bring money home. Now the rate is 15.5%. The difference works out to about $24 billion in incremental cash to be made available for buybacks.
Combined with Apple’s existing spending on shares, that means the company could purchase $173 billion of its stock over the next three years, with the largest portion of the spending front-loaded into this year. That assumes flattish free cash flow and a 5% yearly dividend increase.
In a cover story last month, Barron’s predicted that Apple will be the first U.S. company to hit $1 trillion in stock market value, implying a share price of about $200, versus a recent $174.80.
